notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics vendor running a 30-day Hosted API trial; now moving to evaluation for Dedicated after performance validation. Trial takeaways: latency for short chat templates good (p95 ~420ms with streaming), heavy tail for larger context prompts (p95 up to 2.4s). Customer says: "Host API was trivial to integrate — low friction. We need predictable unit costs and isolation for customer data as we move to enterprise customers."

Key customer asks (shorthand):
- Dedicated sizing guidance for launch (50k MAU), steady-state (150k MAU), and 12‑month growth.
- Forecasts broken down by endpoint (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) and token mix.
- Pricing model: committed capacity + overage vs pure usage for first year.
- Security: SOC2 evidence, SSO, KMS integration, residency for EU customers.

Internal notes: SE ran sample traffic replay from Hosted API logs (anonymized) and provided a baseline throughput profile (see qps_forecast and token_mix). Customer is risk-averse about cold-start latency and wants canary + automatic fallback to Hosted in case Dedicated saturates. They asked for a simple failover policy and price for cross-region fallback.
timeline: 2024-11-12 - Intro call (Jordan, Maya) - scoped use cases and compliance needs.
2024-12-03 - SE perf review: initial traffic replay + token analysis provided.
2024-12-07 - Customer asks for Dedicated sizing + pricing.
qps_forecast:
Derived from 30-day Hosted API trial logs (anonymized):
- Target launch (month 1): peak QPS 45 (10:00-11:00 PST peak), sustained average 18 QPS.
- Steady state (6 months): average 25 QPS, peak 80 QPS with marketing-driven bursts.
- Endpoint split (QPS share): chat 55% (avg call rate), embeddings 30% (short requests but high volume), reranking 15%.
- Concurrency target: 35 concurrent generation streams during peak (chat generation), caching & batching assumed for embeddings to reduce GPU load.
Note: forecasts assume 10% weekly growth for first 12 weeks post-launch.
token_mix:
Observed token characteristics from trial:
- Chat: 55% of traffic, avg tokens per request 420 (prompt ~120 + generation ~300).
- Embeddings: 30% of traffic, avg tokenized input ~250 tokens (short docs, batched requests typical).
- Reranking: 15% of traffic, avg tokens per request ~90.
- Weighted average tokens per request (all endpoints): ~310 tokens.
Implication: chat generation dominates GPU cycles; embeddings contribute more memory/bandwidth but are cheaper per request when batched.
dedicated_capacity_request:
Customer requested a recommended Dedicated starting configuration: two sizing options to review.
- Minimum (cost-conscious): 2 x A100-80GB instances (pool w/ autoscale + burst) — estimated to handle sustained 25 QPS and occasional burst to 50 QPS with increased latency on the tail.
- Recommended (performance-first): 4 x A100-80GB (or H100-equivalent) with KV prefix caching + batching for embeddings — supports steady 50+ QPS, peak bursts to 120 QPS with p95 chat latency target <700ms.
Notes: SE to model batching settings (max_batch_size 8-16), prefix cache hit target 30% for conversational reuse. Customer asked for a runbook showing how fallback to Hosted happens when pool is saturated.
pricing_notes: Customer expects a blended price negotiation: committed monthly capacity for first 12 months (discounted) + usage overage. They asked for examples: 20% discount for 12-month commit vs on-demand; incremental discount tiers if ARR crosses $250k. Request: provide 3 pricing scenarios (self-serve commitment, mid-tier enterprise commit, reserved enterprise).
poC_notes:
POC requirements: 1) Dedicated demo with their anonymized replay (SE-owned), 2) SAML SSO test in staging, 3) encryption-in-transit + KMS key exchange test. Success criteria: p95 latency target met for chat at launch load, embeddings throughput >300 reqs/s when batched, and no PII logged in control plane.
